headline: DecisionRAG uses hierarchical decisions for retrieval without a first-stage retriever
summary: A Cornell and ASAPP preprint introduces DecisionRAG, which navigates a document hierarchy by scoring candidate branches with shared-context decision-model judgments rather than relying on a conventional first-stage retriever at query time. Across four author-run benchmarks, the paper reports rank-one gains over selected dense-retrieval pipelines with an 8B reranker, including 13.8 percentage points on MultiDoc2Dial and 17.4 points on Natural Questions. Reported query latency is 0.68–1.76 seconds and API cost 0.22–2.33 cents across the benchmark configurations. These are preprint-reported measurements; independent reproduction and transfer remain open. Navigation prunes branches irreversibly, so poor hierarchies or low exploration budgets can lose relevant evidence.
